VIDEO.title: Why Paul Says 'No One Is Good' (Romans 3 Explained)
VIDEO.series: The Book of Romans, Every Word (playlist of 28 videos)

kicker: Study aid · Romans 3:9-31 · Episode 6 (#6 of 28 in the playlist)
hand: So that grace can open hearts
SUMMARY: The teacher reads Romans 3:9-31. Jews and Greeks are all under sin; Paul strings together Scriptures to show 'There is none righteous, not even one' (3:10-18). The Law speaks to those under it so that every mouth is shut and the whole world is accountable to God (3:19-20). But now the righteousness of God has been manifested through faith in Jesus Christ, whom God displayed publicly as a propitiation (3:21-26). Boasting is excluded; God is the God of Jews and Gentiles; faith does not abolish the Law but establishes it (3:27-31).

Recap: Paul has been leveling the field between Christians from a Jewish background (the teacher's shorthand, CJB) and from a Gentile background (CGB). 'The central focus of this letter is God. Period.' Who God is, what He has done, and what He promises through His covenant faithfulness.

The teacher, born in Samoa in the South Pacific, raises the question of the person who never heard the gospel: Romans 1-3 leaves no one able to say 'I didn't know.' He counts six negatives in 3:10-12 and, recalling gematria from the Matthew study, reads six as the number of sinful mankind.

In 3:19 Paul anticipates a Jewish-background reply ('those verses are about Gentiles'): the Law speaks to those under the Law. The Psalms show Israel too lacks understanding. The word for 'insight' in Psalm 14:2 shares the root sakal with Genesis 3:6, 'desirable to make one wise.' No one understands because no one seeks God; compare Deuteronomy 32:28-29, Isaiah 1:3, 6:9-10, 27:11, Jeremiah 4:22 and Daniel 9:13.

God's righteousness appears four times in 3:21-26: God Himself is acting to redeem. Propitiation (hilasterion) means turning aside God's wrath; C. H. Dodd argued for 'expiation,' cleansing from sin. The teacher says the Jewish mindset holds both, pointing to the mercy seat (Exodus 25:17-22) where the high priest sprinkled blood on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16).

The lesson: 'God's expectations should shut his people's mouths in humility so that his grace can open their hearts in love.' If the Law humbles everyone, grace can unite them. He applies it to high-church and low-church believers looking down on each other and to quarrels over secondary matters (end times, election, politics), asking how we are straining out gnats and swallowing camels today (see Matthew 23:24).
QUOTES: God's expectations should shut his people's mouths in humility so that his grace can open their hearts in love.
The central focus of this letter is God. Period.
If the law humbles everyone, then God's grace can unite them together.
How are we straining out gnats and inadvertently swallowing camels today?

In this is love, not that we have loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son to be the propitiation for our sins.

left.text: as it is written, / “There is none righteous, not even one; / There is none who understands, / There is none who seeks for God; / All have turned aside, together they have become worthless; / There is none who does good, / There is not even one.”

right.text: Yahweh looks down from heaven upon the sons of men / To see if there is anyone who has insight, / Anyone who seeks after God. / They have all turned aside, altogether they have become worthless; / There is no one who does good, not even one.

lines.text: Paul has charged that 'both Jews and Greeks are all under sin' (Romans 3:9). He quotes Psalm 14:1-3 (also Psalm 53:1-3). The teacher counts six negatives in 3:10-12 and reads six as the number of sinful mankind.

No one understands because no one seeks God. The teacher ties the Hebrew behind 'insight' to the same root, sakal, as Genesis 3:6, where the tree was 'desirable to make one wise': the psalmist echoes the fall.

left.text: “Their throat is an open tomb, / With their tongues they keep deceiving,” / “The poison of asps is under their lips”; / “Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness”; / “Their feet are swift to shed blood,

right.text: Their feet run to evil, / And they are quick to shed innocent blood; / Their thoughts are thoughts of wickedness; / Devastation and destruction are in their highways. / They do not know the way of peace, / And there is no justice in their tracks; / They have made their paths crooked, / Whoever treads on them does not know peace.

lines.text: Paul moves through the body: throat (Psalm 5:9), tongue, lips (Psalm 140:3), mouth (Psalm 10:7), feet (Isaiah 59:7-8), eyes (Psalm 36:1). The video also points to Jeremiah 5:16, 'Their quiver is like an open grave.'
Study note (added): Paul closes the chain with 'There is no fear of God before their eyes' (Romans 3:18). The root problem under all the others is not fearing God.

left.text: Now we know that whatever the Law says, it speaks to those who are in the Law, so that every mouth may be shut and all the world may become accountable to God; because by the works of the Law no flesh will be justified in His sight, for through the Law comes the knowledge of sin.

right.text: He said, “Go, and tell this people: / ‘Keep on hearing, but do not understand; / Keep on seeing, but do not know.’

lines.text: Paul anticipates a Jewish-background reply: 'Those verses are about the Gentiles.' No: whatever the Law says, it says to those under it. The Scriptures say Israel too lacked understanding: 'there is no discernment in them' (Deuteronomy 32:28); 'Israel does not know' (Isaiah 1:3); 'they are not a people of discernment' (Isaiah 27:11); 'have no understanding' (Jeremiah 4:22).
Jesus quotes Isaiah 6 to explain the parables: 'while seeing they do not see' (Matthew 13:13). The teacher links it to the soils of Matthew 13.

src.text: But now apart from the Law the righteousness of God has been manifested, being witnessed by the Law and the Prophets, even the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all those who believe; for there is no distinction;

lines.text: The teacher counts God's righteousness four times in 3:21-26 (verses 21, 22, 25 and 26). God is actively redeeming. 'For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, being justified as a gift by His grace' (Romans 3:23-24).
This picks up 1:17: the righteousness of God revealed from God's faithfulness to the faith of those who respond.

left.text: whom God displayed publicly as a propitiation in His blood through faith, for a demonstration of His righteousness, because in the forbearance of God He passed over the sins previously committed;

right.text: There I will meet with you; and from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim which are upon the ark of the testimony, I will speak to you about all which I will command you for the sons of Israel.

lines.text: Propitiation (hilasterion) is usually defined as appeasing God's wrath, which the teacher says is true. C. H. Dodd argued for 'expiation,' cleansing or removal of sin, which the teacher says is also true. In the Jewish mindset it is both.

The word takes us to the mercy seat on the ark, where the high priest sprinkled the blood of the bull and the goat (Leviticus 16:14-16). The Greek Old Testament uses hilasterion for the mercy seat, as does Hebrews 9:5.

left.text: for the demonstration of His righteousness at the present time, so that He would be just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus.

right.text: In this is love, not that we have loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son to be the propitiation for our sins.

lines.text: God is not lenient with sin when He passes over it; the cross shows He is just, and He justifies the one who has faith in Jesus. John adds the motive: love. 'We love, because He first loved us' (1 John 4:19).

src.text: Where then is boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law? Of works? No, but by a law of faith. For we maintain that a man is justified by faith apart from works of the Law.

lines.text: If the Law humbles everyone, no group can look down on another. Boasting is shut out by the same faith that justifies.
Study note (added): 'For no one living is righteous in Your sight' (Psalm 143:2) stands behind Romans 3:20.

left.text: Or is God the God of Jews only? Is He not the God of Gentiles also? Yes, of Gentiles also, since indeed God, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through that faith, is one.

right.text: “Hear, O Israel! Yahweh is our God, Yahweh is one!

lines.text: One God, one way of justification: circumcised and uncircumcised alike by faith. This is the level field the teacher sees Paul building for the Roman church.
Study note (added): Paul echoes the Shema, Israel's daily confession (Deuteronomy 6:4). The oneness of God becomes the ground for one people.

src.text: Do we then abolish the Law through faith? May it never be! On the contrary, we establish the Law.

lines.text: Faith does not throw out the Law; it puts the Law in its proper place. The Law gives knowledge of sin (3:20) and bears witness to the righteousness of God (3:21).
Study note (added): Paul will show how in Romans 4, where the Law's own story of Abraham proves justification by faith.

Answerable to God as Judge, with no defense left (Romans 3:19).

BACKGROUND.p: Romans 3:10-18 strings together lines from Psalms 14 (or 53), 5, 140, 10 and 36 and Isaiah 59. Jewish teachers often linked texts by shared words; here the link is the body: throat, tongue, lips, mouth, feet, eyes.

BACKGROUND.h: The mercy seat and the Day of Atonement
BACKGROUND.p: The mercy seat was the gold cover of the ark, between the cherubim, where God said 'There I will meet with you' (Exodus 25:22). Once a year the high priest sprinkled the blood of a bull and a goat on it (Leviticus 16:14-16). The Greek Old Testament calls it hilasterion, the word Paul uses in Romans 3:25.

In the 1930s C. H. Dodd argued that the hilaskomai word group means expiation (cleansing sin), not propitiation (turning aside wrath). Leon Morris and others replied that the context of God's wrath (Romans 1:18) requires propitiation. Many now say, as the video does, that both ideas are present.

Gematria assigns number values to letters; number symbolism (six as the number of man, as in Revelation 13:18) is a later interpretive tradition. Paul does not comment on the count; the video offers it as a Jewish-flavored reading.

WITNESSES.text: For the phrase, that every mouth may be stopped, is the language of a person hinting at them, although he has not stated it clearly, so as to prevent the language being too harsh.
WITNESSES.src: Homilies on Romans 7, on 3:19. NPNF 1.11 (public domain).

WITNESSES.text: And for this same reason he calls it a propitiation, to show that if the type had such force, much more would the reality display the same.
WITNESSES.src: Homilies on Romans 7, on 3:25. NPNF 1.11 (public domain).

WITNESSES.text: Doubt not then: for it is not of works, but of faith: and shun not the righteousness of God, for it is a blessing in two ways; because it is easy, and also open to all men.
WITNESSES.src: Homilies on Romans 7, on 3:21-24. NPNF 1.11 (public domain).

DEBATES.p: The video affirms both: blood that cleanses sin (expiation) and turns aside God's wrath (propitiation). Dodd denied the wrath element; most evangelical scholars, following Morris, hold it is central. Some translations hedge with 'sacrifice of atonement.'

DEBATES.h: Faith in Christ, or Christ's faithfulness? (3:22)
DEBATES.p: The Greek phrase can be read as faith directed to Christ (LSB) or as Christ's own faithfulness. The video's 'God's faithfulness drawing out man's faith' fits either reading; scholars are divided.

The video stresses that Romans 1-3 leaves no one able to plead ignorance. Christians differ on how God judges those who never heard the gospel; Paul's own answer to the problem is mission (Romans 10:14-15).

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: The count of six negatives holds for the LSB of 3:10-12 ('none' four times, 'not even one' twice). Reading six as the number of sinful mankind is the video's symbolic interpretation, not something Paul says.
Jeremiah 5:16 ('Their quiver is like an open grave') is a verbal parallel; the line Paul quotes in 3:13 is Psalm 5:9.

In the LSB, Psalm 14:2 reads 'anyone who has insight'; the LSB's word tagging does not mark that word, so the sakal link is checked here against Genesis 3:6 and Deuteronomy 32:29, where the LSB tags it.
CJB and CGB are the video's own shorthand, not terms from scholarship.

QUESTIONS: Which line of Romans 3:10-18 do you find hardest to apply to yourself?
Why does Paul insist the Law speaks to those under it (3:19)?
Propitiation and expiation: why might Paul need both ideas?
Where do you see believers looking down on other believers today?
What 'gnats' are you straining while missing weightier things?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: 'God's expectations should shut his people's mouths in humility so that his grace can open their hearts in love.' If the Law humbles everyone, grace can unite everyone. The teacher sees the Roman problem today when high-church congregations look down on low-church ones and the reverse, and when believers divide over secondary matters such as end times, election or politics. He is not talking about correcting real heresy, which matters. But everyone stands on equal footing: equally sinful, equally in need of grace, equally justified only by the blood of Christ. He asks how we strain out gnats and swallow camels (Matthew 23:24), and admits his own past habit of harsh criticism, now replaced by gratitude for undeserved grace.
APPLICATION_ADDED: Study note (added): name one Christian tradition or group you tend to look down on. This week, pray for them by name, and read Romans 3:22-24 aloud as a reminder that 'there is no distinction.'

## None righteous, not even one
1. Romans 3:10-12; Psalm 14:1-3: None righteous, not even one
   Paul (Romans 3:10-12, LSB): "as it is written, / “There is none righteous, not even one; / There is none who understands, / There is none who seeks for God; / All have turned aside, together they have become worthless; / There is none who does good, / There is not even one.”"
   David (Psalm 14:2-3, LSB): "Yahweh looks down from heaven upon the sons of men / To see if there is anyone who has insight, / Anyone who seeks after God. / They have all turned aside, altogether they have become worthless; / There is no one who does good, not even one."
   (video) Paul has charged that 'both Jews and Greeks are all under sin' (Romans 3:9). He quotes Psalm 14:1-3 (also Psalm 53:1-3). The teacher counts six negatives in 3:10-12 and reads six as the number of sinful mankind.

2. Romans 3:13-18; Psalm 5:9; Isaiah 59:7-8: Throat, tongue, lips, feet
   Paul (Romans 3:13-15, LSB): "“Their throat is an open tomb, / With their tongues they keep deceiving,” / “The poison of asps is under their lips”; / “Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness”; / “Their feet are swift to shed blood,"

3. Romans 3:19-20; Isaiah 6:9-10: Every mouth shut
   Paul (Romans 3:19-20, LSB): "Now we know that whatever the Law says, it speaks to those who are in the Law, so that every mouth may be shut and all the world may become accountable to God; because by the works of the Law no flesh will be justified in His sight, for through the Law comes the knowledge of sin."

The Scriptures say Israel too lacked understanding: 'there is no discernment in them' (Deuteronomy 32:28); 'Israel does not know' (Isaiah 1:3); 'they are not a people of discernment' (Isaiah 27:11); 'have no understanding' (Jeremiah 4:22). (Deuteronomy 32:28-29; Isaiah 1:3; Isaiah 27:11; Jeremiah 4:22; Daniel 9:13)

## The righteousness of God and the mercy seat
1. Romans 3:21-24: But now
   God's righteousness, four times Romans 3:21-22: "But now apart from the Law the righteousness of God has been manifested, being witnessed by the Law and the Prophets, even the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all those who believe; for there is no distinction;" https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Romans+3:21-22
   (video) The teacher counts God's righteousness four times in 3:21-26 (verses 21, 22, 25 and 26). God is actively redeeming. 'For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, being justified as a gift by His grace' (Romans 3:23-24). (Romans 3:23-24)
   (video) This picks up 1:17: the righteousness of God revealed from God's faithfulness to the faith of those who respond. (Romans 1:17)
2. Romans 3:25; Exodus 25:21-22: A propitiation in His blood
   Paul (Romans 3:25, LSB): "whom God displayed publicly as a propitiation in His blood through faith, for a demonstration of His righteousness, because in the forbearance of God He passed over the sins previously committed;"
   Yahweh to Moses (Exodus 25:22, LSB): "There I will meet with you; and from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim which are upon the ark of the testimony, I will speak to you about all which I will command you for the sons of Israel."
   (video) Propitiation (hilasterion) is usually defined as appeasing God's wrath, which the teacher says is true. C. H. Dodd argued for 'expiation,' cleansing or removal of sin, which the teacher says is also true. In the Jewish mindset it is both.
   (video) The word takes us to the mercy seat on the ark, where the high priest sprinkled the blood of the bull and the goat (Leviticus 16:14-16). The Greek Old Testament uses hilasterion for the mercy seat, as does Hebrews 9:5. (Leviticus 16:14-16; Hebrews 9:5)
3. Romans 3:26; 1 John 4:10: Just and the justifier
   Paul (Romans 3:26, LSB): "for the demonstration of His righteousness at the present time, so that He would be just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus."
   John (1 John 4:10, LSB): "In this is love, not that we have loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son to be the propitiation for our sins."
   (video) God is not lenient with sin when He passes over it; the cross shows He is just, and He justifies the one who has faith in Jesus. John adds the motive: love. 'We love, because He first loved us' (1 John 4:19). (1 John 4:19)

## Boasting excluded, one God for all
1. Romans 3:27-28: Where then is boasting?
   Excluded Romans 3:27-28: "Where then is boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law? Of works? No, but by a law of faith. For we maintain that a man is justified by faith apart from works of the Law." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Romans+3:27-28
   (video) If the Law humbles everyone, no group can look down on another. Boasting is shut out by the same faith that justifies.
   [Background] Study note (added): 'For no one living is righteous in Your sight' (Psalm 143:2) stands behind Romans 3:20. (Psalm 143:2)
2. Romans 3:29-30; Deuteronomy 6:4: The God of Gentiles also
   Paul (Romans 3:29-30, LSB): "Or is God the God of Jews only? Is He not the God of Gentiles also? Yes, of Gentiles also, since indeed God, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through that faith, is one."
   Moses (Deuteronomy 6:4, LSB): "“Hear, O Israel! Yahweh is our God, Yahweh is one!"
   (video) One God, one way of justification: circumcised and uncircumcised alike by faith. This is the level field the teacher sees Paul building for the Roman church.
   [Background] Study note (added): Paul echoes the Shema, Israel's daily confession (Deuteronomy 6:4). The oneness of God becomes the ground for one people.
3. Romans 3:31: We establish the Law
   May it never be! Romans 3:31: "Do we then abolish the Law through faith? May it never be! On the contrary, we establish the Law." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Romans+3:31
   (video) Faith does not throw out the Law; it puts the Law in its proper place. The Law gives knowledge of sin (3:20) and bears witness to the righteousness of God (3:21).
   [Background] Study note (added): Paul will show how in Romans 4, where the Law's own story of Abraham proves justification by faith. (Romans 4:3)

## Key people
- Paul: Strings Scriptures together to prove all are under sin, then announces the righteousness of God through faith. [Background] Writing to a mixed church in Rome, probably from Corinth.
- David: Psalm 14 (and 53), quoted in 3:10-12; Psalms 5, 140, 10 and 36 supply more lines. [Background] Psalms 14, 53, 5, 140 and 36 bear David's name in their headings.
- Isaiah: Isaiah 59:7-8 in 3:15-17; Isaiah 1, 6 and 27 on Israel's lack of understanding. [Background] Isaiah 6:9-10 is quoted by Jesus in Matthew 13 and by Paul in Acts 28.
- Eve: Saw that the tree was desirable to make one wise (Genesis 3:6); the teacher links the word to Psalm 14:2. [Background] Genesis 3 is the background for Paul's Adam-and-Christ argument in Romans 5.
- Moses and Aaron: The mercy seat (Exodus 25) and the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16), where the high priest sprinkled blood. [Background] Aaron, the first high priest, entered the holy of holies once a year (Leviticus 16:2, 34).
- C. H. Dodd: Argued that hilasterion should be translated 'expiation' rather than 'propitiation.' [Background] Welsh New Testament scholar (1884-1973). Leon Morris answered him, defending 'propitiation.'

## Places [Background]
- Jerusalem: The temple, whose holy of holies once held the ark and its mercy seat.
- Mount Sinai: Where Moses received the pattern for the ark and the mercy seat (traditional site).
- Rome: The church of Jews and Gentiles that Paul addresses.
- Corinth: Where Paul probably wrote Romans.

## Key terms
- Under sin: Under sin's power and guilt, as a ruling condition, not only individual acts (Romans 3:9). [Background]
- Accountable: Answerable to God as Judge, with no defense left (Romans 3:19).
- Righteousness of God: God's own righteousness, now revealed and given through faith in Jesus Christ (Romans 3:21-22).
- Justified: Declared righteous by God, as a gift by His grace (Romans 3:24).
- Redemption: Release by payment of a price; set free (Romans 3:24). [Background]
- Propitiation: A sacrifice that turns aside God's wrath; the Greek word also names the mercy seat (Romans 3:25).
- Expiation: Cleansing or removal of sin; C. H. Dodd's preferred rendering of hilasterion.
- Mercy seat: The gold cover of the ark between the cherubim, sprinkled with blood on the Day of Atonement (Exodus 25:17-22).
- Forbearance: God's patient holding back of judgment on sins previously committed (Romans 3:25). [Background]

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- A chain of quotations: Romans 3:10-18 strings together lines from Psalms 14 (or 53), 5, 140, 10 and 36 and Isaiah 59. Jewish teachers often linked texts by shared words; here the link is the body: throat, tongue, lips, mouth, feet, eyes.
- The mercy seat and the Day of Atonement: The mercy seat was the gold cover of the ark, between the cherubim, where God said 'There I will meet with you' (Exodus 25:22). Once a year the high priest sprinkled the blood of a bull and a goat on it (Leviticus 16:14-16). The Greek Old Testament calls it hilasterion, the word Paul uses in Romans 3:25.
- Propitiation or expiation?: In the 1930s C. H. Dodd argued that the hilaskomai word group means expiation (cleansing sin), not propitiation (turning aside wrath). Leon Morris and others replied that the context of God's wrath (Romans 1:18) requires propitiation. Many now say, as the video does, that both ideas are present.
- Gematria and the number six: Gematria assigns number values to letters; number symbolism (six as the number of man, as in Revelation 13:18) is a later interpretive tradition. Paul does not comment on the count; the video offers it as a Jewish-flavored reading.

## Early witnesses [Background: sourced]
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 391): "For the phrase, that every mouth may be stopped, is the language of a person hinting at them, although he has not stated it clearly, so as to prevent the language being too harsh." Homilies on Romans 7, on 3:19. NPNF 1.11 (public domain).
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 391): "And for this same reason he calls it a propitiation, to show that if the type had such force, much more would the reality display the same." Homilies on Romans 7, on 3:25. NPNF 1.11 (public domain).
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 391): "Doubt not then: for it is not of works, but of faith: and shun not the righteousness of God, for it is a blessing in two ways; because it is easy, and also open to all men." Homilies on Romans 7, on 3:21-24. NPNF 1.11 (public domain).

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- Propitiation or expiation? The video affirms both: blood that cleanses sin (expiation) and turns aside God's wrath (propitiation). Dodd denied the wrath element; most evangelical scholars, following Morris, hold it is central. Some translations hedge with 'sacrifice of atonement.'
- Faith in Christ, or Christ's faithfulness? (3:22) The Greek phrase can be read as faith directed to Christ (LSB) or as Christ's own faithfulness. The video's 'God's faithfulness drawing out man's faith' fits either reading; scholars are divided.
- The person who never heard The video stresses that Romans 1-3 leaves no one able to plead ignorance. Christians differ on how God judges those who never heard the gospel; Paul's own answer to the problem is mission (Romans 10:14-15).

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- The count of six negatives holds for the LSB of 3:10-12 ('none' four times, 'not even one' twice). Reading six as the number of sinful mankind is the video's symbolic interpretation, not something Paul says.
- Jeremiah 5:16 ('Their quiver is like an open grave') is a verbal parallel; the line Paul quotes in 3:13 is Psalm 5:9.
- In the LSB, Psalm 14:2 reads 'anyone who has insight'; the LSB's word tagging does not mark that word, so the sakal link is checked here against Genesis 3:6 and Deuteronomy 32:29, where the LSB tags it.
- CJB and CGB are the video's own shorthand, not terms from scholarship.

1. Which line of Romans 3:10-18 do you find hardest to apply to yourself?
2. Why does Paul insist the Law speaks to those under it (3:19)?

5. What 'gnats' are you straining while missing weightier things?

## Application
- (video) 'God's expectations should shut his people's mouths in humility so that his grace can open their hearts in love.' If the Law humbles everyone, grace can unite everyone. The teacher sees the Roman problem today when high-church congregations look down on low-church ones and the reverse, and when believers divide over secondary matters such as end times, election or politics. He is not talking about correcting real heresy, which matters. But everyone stands on equal footing: equally sinful, equally in need of grace, equally justified only by the blood of Christ. He asks how we strain out gnats and swallow camels (Matthew 23:24), and admits his own past habit of harsh criticism, now replaced by gratitude for undeserved grace.
- Study note (added): name one Christian tradition or group you tend to look down on. This week, pray for them by name, and read Romans 3:22-24 aloud as a reminder that 'there is no distinction.'
